title: Algebraic quotient and fppf presentation of a flat groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $U,R$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with source and target maps $s,t:R\to U$, identity $e:U\to R$, inverse $i:R\to R$ and composition $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$. Assume these induce, naturally on every test scheme, a groupoid with object set $U(T)$ and arrow set $R(T)$: identities, inverse and associative composition satisfy the category laws. Assume $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, with these properties tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\mathcal Q$ be the stackification of this groupoid on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], and let $p:U\to\mathcal Q$ be the object map. Then $\mathcal Q$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Its diagonal and $p$ are representable by algebraic spaces; $p$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective. Surjective means that every target object over a field lifts after a field extension. The arrow map induces an equivalence $R\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$, with the projections given by source and target. Here a $2$-fibre product has objects consisting of a pair and an isomorphism between their images [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

proof.text: For $u,v\in U(T)$ the arrow presheaf is $I_{u,v}=T\times_{(u,v),U\times_SU,(s,t)}R$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], regarding schemes as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Hence it is an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The Isom clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] identifies $\operatorname{Isom}(p(u),p(v))$ with its sheafification, which is itself by the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. All identifications respect restriction and the arrow map. Algebraic spaces over $S$ equipped with a map to a scheme $T$ are algebraic spaces over $T$: on slice tests their same etale charts and diagonal tests check the definition directly.

Objects of $U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$ over $T$ are triples $(u,v,\alpha:p(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}p(v))$. Step 1 gives a unique $r\in R(T)$ with $s(r)=u$, $t(r)=v$ and image $\alpha$. Both U factors have only identity arrows, so these triples have only identity arrows as well. These bijections commute with pullback and prove the arrow-map equivalence, with projections s and t.

For $a,b\in\mathcal Q(T)$, stackification supplies an fppf covering on which both are isomorphic to $p(u_i),p(v_i)$; use successive coverings and the site axioms [def-pc-fppf-site]. Conjugation by these isomorphisms identifies their Isom sheaf locally with $I_{u_i,v_i}$ of step 1. This is a sheaf because Q is a stack. Choose the covering index and etale charts in the working Grothendieck universe [def-weil-size-convention]; their scheme coproduct exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and lies in the ambient big site. Thus the chart-size hypothesis of [lem-sfb-fppf-local-algebraic-space] holds. That lemma makes the Isom sheaf an algebraic space. The pullback of the diagonal by $(a,b):T\to\mathcal Q\times_S\mathcal Q$ is exactly this sheaf, since its objects are isomorphisms from a to b. Hence the diagonal is representable. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] with A=U to obtain representability of p.

We may apply algebraic-stack morphism calculus to algebraic spaces themselves, independently of Q. Indeed an algebraic space is an fppf sheaf, hence a discrete fppf stack by unique gluing. Its diagonal is representable by schemes by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its surjective etale scheme chart is a representable etale surjection in the fibred-groupoid sense by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], and therefore smooth by the same node. These are the conditions of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Any morphism between algebraic spaces is representable by algebraic spaces, again by the fibred-groupoid calculus. The chart hypothesis on $s$ gives flatness and local finite presentation in this representable sense: choose an etale scheme chart $V\to U$ and an etale scheme chart $W\to R\times_{s,U}V$. By the composition and base-change clauses of the fibred-groupoid calculus, $W\to R$ is an etale scheme chart of $R$ over $V$, so $W\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. Both charts are surjective flat locally finitely presented covers, since representable etale maps are smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The last clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] therefore makes $s$ flat and locally of finite presentation; with identity charts the same clause applies to morphisms of schemes. Consequently [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] gives arbitrary base-change stability of flatness and local finite presentation for such maps, including s.

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathcal Q(T)$. Step 3 gives an algebraic space $F=U\times_{\mathcal Q}T$. Choose an fppf covering $T_i\to T$ with $q|_{T_i}\simeq p(v_i)$ by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Describe F using pairs $(u,\alpha:q\to p(u))$. Composition with $p(v_i)\to q$ and step 1 identify $F\times_TT_i$ with $R\times_{s,U,v_i}T_i$, whose projection is flat and locally of finite presentation by step 4. It is surjective because $z\mapsto(e(v_i(z)),z)$ is a section. This is a scheme-base-change calculation and makes no smoothness or algebraicity assumption on Q.

source.place: Tag 06FH (lemma-flat-quotient-flat-presentation), local calculation and identity section.

proof.text: Let $T^\prime=\coprod_iT_i$, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. The map $T^\prime\to T$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation: the covering maps have these properties by [def-pc-fppf-site], and flatness and local finite presentation are local on its disjoint open cover by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to schemes as in step 4. The map $F\times_TT^\prime\to T^\prime$ has these two properties because its restrictions are the maps in step 5; the same calculus gives this on their open cover. Apply the algebraic-space case of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to $F\to T$ and this cover to descend both properties. Surjectivity descends directly: for a field-valued point of T, choose a covering point over it after field extension, and then use the section in step 5 to obtain a point of F after that extension. Thus every base change of p is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective.

By [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], Q is an fppf stack. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-stack-algebraicity-bootstrap] with A=U, Y=Q and f=p. U is an algebraic space by hypothesis, step 3 gives representability, and steps 5-6 give every scheme-base-change projection flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective. The criterion gives an algebraic stack with a smooth scheme atlas. Step 3 supplies its representable diagonal, step 6 the required properties of p, and step 2 the arrow-map equivalence with its stated projections. These prove all clauses.
